learningObjectives: Explain why Java projects use build and dependency management tools.
Identify the major components of a Maven or Gradle project.
Construct a basic dependency and build workflow.

activities.title: Build Tool Concepts
activities.instruction: Explore what the major build-tool features do.

content.concept: Java build tools automate tasks such as dependency resolution, compilation, testing, packaging, and running project-specific build tasks.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Resolves and makes external libraries available to the project.
Converts Java source code into compiled class files.
Runs automated tests as part of the build.
Produces distributable artifacts such as JAR files.
Defines how project tasks and plugins are executed.

activities.title: Maven Project Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the important parts of a Maven project.

content.concept: A Maven project commonly uses pom.xml for project metadata, dependencies, plugins, and build configuration, while source and test code follow conventional directory structures.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Defines project metadata, dependencies, plugins, and build configuration.
Contains the main Java source code.
Contains application resources used at runtime.
Commonly contains generated build output and packaged artifacts.

activities.title: Dependency Builder
activities.instruction: Build the essential structure of a Maven dependency.

content.concept: A Maven dependency identifies an external library using coordinates such as groupId, artifactId, and version so Maven can resolve it for the project.

activities.title: Build Workflow
activities.instruction: Arrange a typical Java build workflow.

content.concept: A build normally resolves dependencies, compiles source code, runs tests, and packages the application into a distributable artifact.
